title: The Cost of Link-Only Culture
author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: The Cost of Link-Only Culture: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: Link-only publication can respect rights, but a culture whose evidence lives only behind unstable links inherits broken memory, platform power, and unequal access.
frames.alt: Title plate for The Cost of Link-Only Culture.

frames.caption: 01 · DEPEND — Which memory exists only elsewhere?. Inventory source URL, platform, account owner, identifier, format, access condition, geography, login, cost, rights, and evidence use.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping which memory exists only elsewhere? within The Cost of Link-Only Culture.

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · PERMIT — What may lawfully be retained?. Separate public visibility, download ability, license, authorized embed, preservation copy, quotation, metadata, and link. Review contracts and jurisdiction where uncertain.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what may lawfully be retained? within The Cost of Link-Only Culture.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · DESCRIBE — What survives without the media?. Write a faithful factual description, creator and institution credit, date, identifier, evidentiary relevance, rights status, and retrieval history without substituting invented imagery.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what survives without the media? within The Cost of Link-Only Culture.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: Preservation rhetoric can become a justification for copying creators’ work without consent. Conversely, rights uncertainty can erase minoritized histories first. The response is resourced permission work, accurate metadata, lawful preservation, and transparent absence.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for The Cost of Link-Only Culture.
frames.treatment: typographic quotation field; no decorative imagery

frames.caption: Classify permitted copy, embed, excerpt, metadata-only, link-only, and no-use.
